cycles to serve more simultaneous users. Traditional Web Application Vs Single page Application Traditional Web Application
Full Page Reloads: Every user action requests a brand-new page. Server-Side Rendering: The web server generates and sends complete HTML pages. Higher Bandwidth: Transferring full HTML documents every time consumes more data. Slower Transitions: The browser blanking out between pages creates a disjointed UX. Single page Application
Dynamic Updates: The page loads once and updates content dynamically without reloading. Client-Side Rendering: An internal HTTP Client manages data fetching and updates the UI. Data-Only Requests: The server sends lightweight JSON data instead of heavy HTML. Desktop-Like UX: Fluid transitions mimic a native desktop or mobile app experience.
